newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE POWER'S 1996/97 NET PROFIT UP 42.8 PCT.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE POWER'S 1996/97 NET PROFIT UP 42.8 PCT.

text.p: State-owned Singapore Power said on Monday its net profit after tax for the financial year 1996/97 rose 42.8 percent to Singapore $771 million.
It said in a statement turnover grew by 13.8 percent with revenue reaching S$3.1 billion. Group assets were $11 billion.
Electricity revenue made up 91 percent of total revenue followed by gas at four percent.
Profits were helped by rises in electricity and gas revenues, which rose 15.1 percent and 8.5 percent respectively as compared with the previous year.
It said about half of the increase in profit before tax was due to productivity gains. The other half was due to increases in sales and tariffs.
Demand for electricity over next few years was expected to grow by about six to seven percent annually, it said.
The company said it had targeted cost savings of S$300 million to S$500 million over the next 10 years.
Some $1 billion in capital expenditure had been set aside, mainly to develop transmission, it said.
It said efforts to diversify, including venturing overseas and investing in telecommunications would intensify in the current financial year.
